Day 1 of 30 · Sentence foundations
about 45 minutes
What every word is doing

Name the job each word performs in a sentence, so that you can see why an error is an error.

WHY THIS MATTERS IN THE PAPER

Error-correction questions never tell you which rule is broken. You are shown a sentence and asked to find the fault. That is only possible if you can see that in “he speaks English fluent”, the word fluent is an adjective standing in an adverb’s place.

HOW TO WORK THIS DAY

1. Read the rules slowly, once.
2. Cover the right-hand column of the examples and predict.
3. Do the warm-up; if you miss one, reread that rule.
4. Attempt the drill and read each explanation.
5. Write the six corrections out by hand.
6. Finish with the writing task in your own words.
WORDS YOU WILL NEED TODAY
Word class (part of speech)
The job a word is doing in a particular sentence - not a permanent label stuck to the word.
Noun
A word that names a person, place, thing, group or idea: officer, Lahore, file, committee, justice.
Verb
A word that carries the action or the state: approve, collapse, seem, is.
Adjective
A word that describes a noun: a weak institution, transparent rules.
Adverb
A word that describes a verb, an adjective or another adverb: acted quickly, deeply unfair.
Function word
A small word that joins or points rather than describes: the, of, and, because, to.
